• expression_2 (consequent): “one cycle later both $fell(c3) and $fell(d3) must occur simultaneously; next, for four consecutive cycles neither c3 nor d3 may be true; then one cycle later both c3 and d3 must be true; and finally, one cycle after that b3 must be true.”  
• Reason:  “|=>” is a binary operator, so we split into the “if” part (expression_1) and the “then” part (expression_2).

3.1  expression_1 is purely a sequence.  
    Translation:  
      $fell(a3) ##[2:5] $fell(b3)

     => ##1 ($fell(c3) and $fell(d3))  

  b) “next, for four consecutive cycles neither c3 nor d3 may be true”  
     => (!$c3 && !d3)[*4]  
     (the [*4] repetition matches exactly four back-to-back cycles of !c3 && !d3)  

  c) “then one cycle later both c3 and d3 must be true”  
     => ##1 (c3 && d3)  

  d) “and finally, one cycle after that b3 must be true”  
     => ##1 b3  

  Chaining them:  
     ##1 ($fell(c3) && $fell(d3))  
    ##1 ((!c3 && !d3)[*4])  
    ##1 (c3 && d3)  
    ##1 b3

      |=>

     ##1 ((!c3 && !d3)[*4])  
     ##1 (c3 && d3)  
     ##1 b3)
